thread.title: UK Economy Expands by 0.1 Percent in August

author: Ahmed Ibrahim World Editor
title: UK Economy Expands by 0.1 Percent in August
text:
Britain’s economy expanded by 0.1 per cent in August, bolstering the Chancellor ahead of the autumn Budget.
Official figures released by the Office for National Statistics revealed momentum in the UK economy during August, following a 0.4 per cent expansion in July. Bank of England Deputy Governor for Financial Stability Sarah Breeden told business news channel CNBC that she had been surprised by the private sector’s stamina.
We’ve been surprised so far about how well the economy has absorbed what has been a pretty significant energy price shock, Breeden said while attending International Monetary Fund meetings in Bangkok. She pointed to a shift in corporate behavior compared with the 2022 energy crisis, noting that businesses today are far more inclined to trim expenses internally rather than pass rising fuel bills directly to shoppers.
Corporate Cost-Cutting Supports the Bank of England’s Inflation Fight The current resilience stems largely from hard lessons learned during prior supply disruptions. Many British firms hedged their energy purchases ahead of recent volatility linked to the conflict in the Middle East, buffering the immediate blow. At the same time, artificial intelligence investments and data-centre development have provided a modest secondary floor for business activity, even if domestic adoption lags behind the United States.
That reluctance to hike consumer prices has kept broader price pressures contained. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, speaking at an Institute of International Finance meeting in Bangkok, noted that above-target UK inflation remains enormously frustrating , yet emphasized that secondary price effects are currently subdued.
Photo: London Business News What’s really different now, relative to when we had the last energy shock in 2022, is that people aren’t looking to push costs through.
Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability at the Bank of England
Breeden added that a softer labor market is helping prevent a recurrence of the aggressive wage increases seen in 2022. While some households face a genuine affordability crunch amid elevated living costs, companies are choosing to absorb the shock rather than fuel an inflationary spiral, easing the monitoring burden for monetary policymakers.
Diverging Central Bank Policies and the November Rate Decision While the European Central Bank and the US Federal Reserve have moved to raise interest rates, the Bank of England has held its policy rate steady since the onset of the Iran war. Financial markets, however, have priced in a near-certain 0.25 percentage point rate increase at the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting.

Bailey warned that the UK economy is more resilient than expected , but still falls short of necessary strength, leaving policymakers watchful for delayed damage as elevated energy costs persist.
